notes.body: New Hampshire is the only U.S. state that doesn't require auto insurance by statute. A financial-responsibility law still applies: if you cause a crash, you must be able to pay for the damage.
notes.title: Insurance isn't required — but responsibility is

notes.body: Purchased policies must carry at least $25,000/$50,000 bodily-injury liability and $25,000 property damage, plus $1,000 in medical payments (MedPay) and 25/50 uninsured-motorist coverage.
notes.title: If you buy, minimums are 25/50/25

notes.body: State minimums only cover damage you cause to others — not your own car or injuries beyond the limits. Many drivers carry higher limits for real protection.
notes.title: Minimums may not be enough

minCoverage.notes: Auto insurance is not required by NH statute; these are the financial-responsibility minimums that apply if you buy a policy or cause an accident.
